title: Balanced Search Invariants and Execution Dynamics in a Ruby Aether-Module for Chronos-Processor Compilers
topic: Libtt: A Compiler and Runtime for Tenstorrent Processors
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a Ruby-based compiler and runtime, Aether-Module, that targets Chronos-Processor architectures. The core of Aether-Module is a height-balanced search tree used for indexing intermediate representations, guaranteeing $O(\log n)$ search, insertion, and deletion. We formally prove that the tree preserves strict height-balance and key-order invariants after each compiler pass. Empirical evaluation on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C system shows a mean latency of 55 681.27 \textmu{}s per graph execution and a throughput of 17 959 ops/s. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/ruby-algorithms-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261128_020156_libtt__a_compiler_and_runtime}
